new_breakage.what: fix_rounds[0].tests holds one run, the fix-diff audit `tools/kb.sh audit --base e7dbc69 --head f03e43c --ids ...`, and it was executed without `--report`. Its summary reads deterministic 10, pass 6, fail 1, skipped 3.
new_breakage.why: That is the batch 12 defect this very task exists to stop: the spec's Facts section names "batch 12's fix-round audit without --report" as one of the two shapes that cost a review round. The new validate check cannot catch it, because it only inspects the top-level self_audit, so the fix round's own evidence is the weaker kind the batch is removing. The three skipped rows are the report-field checks, so the fix diff was never checked against process.deliverables-json, process.knowledge-first or security-hygiene.verify-current-docs.
new_breakage.fix: Re-run the fix-diff audit as `tools/kb.sh audit --base e7dbc69 --head f03e43c --ids <the eight Knowledge ids> --report .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-04-batch-14/task-1-report.json` and replace fix_rounds[0].tests[0] with the run that shows skipped 0. Keep the top-level audit at tests[6] as it is; it already covers c7db95e..f03e43c with --report.

new_breakage.what: The section heading still reads `## Before answering: validate, self-audit, self-review`, but the steps under it now run in the order audit and fill (step 1), validate (step 2), self-review (step 3). The heading named the old order and was correct before this round.
new_breakage.why: The heading is the first line an implementer reads for the closing sequence. A heading that lists the steps in the opposite order to the list under it invites the agent to validate first, which is the state the round just removed.
new_breakage.fix: Rename the heading to the order the steps now run, for example `## Before answering: self-audit, validate, self-review`, in template/.claude/agents/implementer.md, then sync the root copy with `node bin/houserules.mjs update --dir .`. This is another implementer.md edit, so the process.evals-rerun fail row stays until T3 pays it.
